# MoveMonkey

> MoveMonkey is a stand-up reminder for iPhone and Apple Watch with a cartoon monkey as its character. It reminds you to get up when you have been sitting too long, and cheers when you do. Chinese store name (Simplified and Traditional): MoveMonkey：久坐提醒 (久坐提醒 means "sedentary reminder", a reminder to get up after sitting too long).

## What it does

- Within the reminder hours you set (08:00 to 21:00 by default), it counts the time since you last got up. Once you have sat for the time you set (30, 45, 60, or 90 minutes; 60 by default), your iPhone sends a notification, and Apple Watch reminds you too if you wear one.
- It reads stand minutes, stand hours, and steps (with your permission, from the Health app and Motion & Fitness) to tell whether you have been up and moving. When it sees that you have, the clock starts over, so moving pushes the next reminder back.
- Get Up: tap it and walk for 1 minute; Apple Watch counts your steps in real time (without Apple Watch, iPhone counts them), and the monkey cheers for you when the minute is up.
- When you start Get Up on iPhone, a Live Activity shows the walk's time on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island.
- Just Moved: tell it you just got up, and the clock starts over.
- Today's stand hours count toward a daily stand goal (10 hours by default); on the day you reach it you earn a banana award. Every day starts at zero.
- Pause reminders for a few hours or for the rest of the day; set a lunch break with no reminders; in the morning it waits until you are up (2 hours at most).
- Works with iPhone alone; Apple Watch is optional.

## What it is not

- Not a medical device; it makes no health claims and gives no medical advice.
- No analytics or tracking code. Health data stays on your devices. To remind you on time, the devices send the developer's server only the reminder times they work out, with a push token (the privacy policy lists everything sent and kept).

## Facts

- Platforms: iPhone with iOS 18 or later; Apple Watch with watchOS 10 or later.
- Languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese.
- Price: the core features are free forever, with no ads.
- Category: Health & Fitness.
- Developer: an independent developer.
- Contact: support@movemonkey.app

How to Get a Reminder Every Half Hour](https://movemonkey.app/en/apple-watch-stand-reminder-30-minutes/): why the stand reminder can’t be set to 30 minutes (it’s on or off, by the clock hour), and six built-in ways to get a reminder every 30 minutes, each with its steps and limits: Chimes (one switch, hourly, 30 or 15 minutes), Mindfulness reminders, a Shortcuts automation (in iOS 27, one shortcut can take several Time of Day triggers), Alarms, Reminders and Timers; MoveMonkey, a stand-up reminder app that reminds you only after you’ve sat for 30 minutes since you last got up; why Mindfulness reminders sometimes don’t come; our tests on watchOS 27.0.1 and iOS 27; none of the built-in ways checks whether you have stood up

- [How Often Should You Get Up from Sitting? Every Hour or Every 30 Minutes](https://movemonkey.app/en/how-often-to-get-up/): what the guidelines say (the Dietary Guidelines for Chinese Residents 2022: get up and move every hour; the American Diabetes Association’s 2026 Standards of Care: interrupt sitting at least every 30 minutes for people with or at risk of diabetes), the studies behind “every 30 minutes”, why getting up and walking helps (contracting muscle takes up blood glucose without insulin; thigh muscles are mostly inactive while sitting; energy cost of sitting, standing and slow walking), the WHO definition of sedentary behavior, how long to walk at each break (a 2-minute slow walk every 20 minutes lowered the post-meal glucose rise by 24%; walking lowered it more than standing), and Canada’s limit of 8 hours of sedentary time a day; every claim cited
- [久坐多久要起来一次？每小时还是每 30 分钟](https://movemonkey.app/how-often-to-get-up/): the same article in Simplified Chinese
- [久坐多久要起來一次？每小時還是每 30 分鐘](https://movemonkey.app/zh-hant/how-often-to-get-up/): the same article in Traditional Chinese
- [How Does Apple Watch Count Stand Hours?](https://movemonkey.app/en/apple-watch-stand-hours/): a stand hour is any clock hour with at least 1 minute of standing and moving (Apple); Stand Minutes vs. stand hours (one Stand Minute in an hour earns the hour); what a 2024 University of Dundee study of 20 users found (an hour with more than about 97.5 steps or 100 kJ of active energy was much more likely to be recorded as a stand hour); Stand vs. Exercise vs. Move rings; what 4/12 means and how to change the Stand goal (6 to 16 hours; by weekday since watchOS 11); why stands go uncounted (fit, Wrist Detection, iPhone alone; users report arm swing matters)
